messages.subject: Growth curve models on percentages
parts:
Greetings all,

I would like to run a Bayesian growth curve model on manifest outcomes that are highly aggregated percentages (percentages at the country level). Data are not available at the individual level.   For the repeated outcomes, I would like to specify them as either uniform(a,b) or beta(shape, scale).  Is this possible?

Thanks in advance,

David

messages.subject: Re: Growth curve models on percentages
parts:
David

No, for now, for continuous outcomes, blavaan only allows to specify them as normal(), or ordered categorical.

How does the histograms look like? Could it be treated as normal, and set string priors to limit the parameter space

How would I set the string priors to specify the distribution of the y's?

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Growth curve models on percentages
parts:
David

As y's are the outcome variables, you cant set a prior on them specifically, because their means are based on the predictions of the model on their means.

Based on the growth model, the item intercepts will be fixed to 0 to identify the factors. So, the means have to be defined at the means of the latent factors. So, if the scores are around 0 and .3, you could set the factor means as

int ~ prior("normal(0.1, 0.2)")*1
 slp ~ prior("normal(0, 0.2)")*1

This will not fully truncate it (dont recommend it), but will define the expected means. You can do a quick visualization with the rnorm function, to see what fits your expectation

hist(rnorm(10000, .2, .2))
